It's understandable to feel confused and frustrated when a family member's behavior shifts dramatically and affects everyone around them. What you're describing—swinging between periods of high energy and very low moods—could reflect a range of things, including mental health conditions that benefit from professional support. It's often hard to know from the outside what someone is truly experiencing, and even behaviors that seem attention-seeking can sometimes signal genuine distress.

Encouraging your mom to speak with a healthcare professional could be a meaningful step. A doctor or mental health provider can properly assess what's going on and recommend appropriate support. You might also find it helpful to talk to someone yourself, as navigating a family member's mental health can be emotionally taxing. If you're in the US, NAMI (1-800-950-6264) offers guidance for family members. Your feelings and well-being matter throughout this process too.
